definitions.o: min(d,c), an upper bound on how many of the d pivot-parent clauses can omit any fixed nonpivot variable
definitions.Wmax_r_R: maximum possible sum of widths of R distinct signed non-tautological clauses over r variables; compute by taking clause widths r,r-1,...,0 with multiplicities C(r,w)2^w

statement: Let a selected pivot have p positive and q negative parent clauses, d=p+q, in a canonical ordinary CNF with n live variables and m clauses. For each nonpivot variable y let a_y,b_y be the number of positive/negative pivot parents omitting y. Minimum-incidence selection implies a_y+b_y<=o=min(d,m-d). Hence total pair-support mass over all pq cross-polarity parent pairs is at least Smin=r*(pq-M(p,q,o)). If R distinct non-tautological resolvents are produced, total pair-support mass is at most Wmax_r(R)+(pq-R)r. Therefore any R satisfying Wmax_r(R)+(pq-R)r<Smin is impossible, and the maximum feasible R gives an exact ceiling on the number of distinct resolvents. Consequently raw_units is at most 1+c+c*r+R+Wmax_r(R), or tighter when a separate retained-literal bound is available.
proof: Because the selected pivot has minimum incidence d, every live nonpivot variable has total incidence at least d.
A nonpivot variable can occur in at most c=m-d retained clauses, so it occurs in at least max(0,d-c) pivot-parent clauses and is omitted from at most d-max(0,d-c)=min(d,c)=o pivot parents.

If a_y positive parents and b_y negative parents omit variable y, then exactly a_y*b_y cross pairs have union-support omitting y. Since a_y+b_y<=o, a_y*b_y<=M(p,q,o). Thus at least pq-M(p,q,o) parent pairs contain y in their union support.
Summing this lower bound over all r nonpivot variables gives total pair-support mass S>=r*(pq-M(p,q,o))=Smin.

For each distinct non-tautological resolvent choose one parent pair that produces it. Its support size equals the resolvent width. Among R distinct signed clauses over r variables, the maximum possible total width is Wmax_r(R).
Every remaining parent pair, whether tautological or duplicating an already-counted resolvent, has union-support size at most r. Hence total pair-support mass is at most Wmax_r(R)+(pq-R)r.

If that upper bound is below Smin, such an R is impossible. Since Wmax_r(R)+(pq-R)r is nonincreasing in R, the largest feasible R is a well-defined exact ceiling and is computable by scanning or binary search over 0<=R<=min(pq,3^r).

The engine raw set contains at most c retained clauses and R distinct resolvents. Retained widths are at most r; distinct resolvent total width is at most Wmax_r(R). Therefore raw_units<=1+c+c*r+R+Wmax_r(R). Canonicalization can only reduce this further.
